title: In Vivo Analysis of Muscle Function in Porcine Models for Muscular Dystrophies
author: Hristov, Blasi, et al.
materials: Aurora 892A Swine Isometric Footplate Test Device

The statistical approach employed in this protocol was tailored to the specific aims and outcome measures of the study. Muscle force was quantified using twitch and tetanus recordings, with five consecutive measurements obtained per animal. To mitigate potential adaptation effects, the initial two recordings were treated as premeasurements for checking the correct fixation and electrode positioning and excluded from the final analysis. Furthermore, inclusion of five measurements per contraction type and animal enables averaging and supports the generation of multiple biological replicates, depending on the analytical strategy.

steps.title: Allocate protocol time
steps.instruction: Reserve approximately 30 minutes for system setup and calibration, 40 minutes for in‑vivo measurements, and one full day for data analysis.

steps.title: Verify system calibration
steps.instruction: Confirm that the Aurora A892 Swine Isometric Footplate Test Device is calibrated by checking system documentation or visible status indicators; if verification fails, stop and contact trained personnel before proceeding.

steps.title: Create new study in software
steps.instruction: Open “File > New Study”, enter a unique study name and a brief description, add Animal ID and Body Weight parameters (assign units and check the “Fixed” box), optionally add Sex, Date of Birth, or Treatment Group, set the muscle group to “Tibialis Anterior”, then save the study.

steps.title: Define Twitch test experiment
steps.instruction: Add a “Twitch” experiment named “Test Twitch”, select Tibialis Anterior, set pulse width to 0.2 ms, click “Customize Experiment”, choose “Timed”, set “Time to Next” to 15 s, set “Repeat” to 4, commit changes, and save the sequence.

steps.title: Define Tetanus test experiment
steps.instruction: Add a “Tetanus” experiment named “Test Tetanus”, ensure Tibialis Anterior is selected, set frequency to 100 Hz and stimulus time to 500 ms, customize to “Timed”, set “Time to Next” to 15 s, set “Repeat” to 2, commit changes, and save.

steps.title: Define Measuring Twitch experiment
steps.instruction: Add another “Twitch” experiment named “Measuring Twitch” with pulse width 0.2 ms, “Timed”, “Time to Next” 15 s, “Repeat” 4, then save.

steps.title: Define Measuring Tetanus experiment
steps.instruction: Add a “Tetanus” experiment named “Measuring Tetanus”, keep frequency 100 Hz and stimulus 500 ms, set repetition to 4, customize as above, and save.

steps.title: Define Force‑Frequency experiment
steps.instruction: Add a “Force Frequency” experiment with 8 steps, frequency range 10–120 Hz (ascending), stimulus time 500 ms, name it “Measuring Force Frequency”, verify Tibialis Anterior is selected, and create the experiment.

steps.title: Define Fatigue experiment
steps.instruction: Add a “Fatigue” experiment named “Measuring Fatigue”, set stimulation frequency to 60 Hz, tetanus duration 500 ms, time between tetani 5000 ms, total duration 10 min, verify muscle selection, and create the experiment.

steps.title: Finalize study setup
steps.instruction: Click “Create Study” to finalize the protocol, ensuring all stimulation values are appropriate to avoid overstimulation or muscle damage.

steps.title: Conduct measurement sequence
steps.instruction: After a 3‑minute rest following test measurements, start the main acquisition: run twitch trials, pause 1 minute, run tetanic trials, rest 3 minutes, run the force‑frequency protocol, pause 5 minutes, run the fatigue protocol, then stop the experiment; all contractions are saved automatically.

steps.title: Post‑measurement animal handling
steps.instruction: Carefully remove stimulation electrodes; if tissue sampling is planned, keep the animal under deep anesthesia and euthanize according to approved protocols; if no sampling is required, allow the animal to recover under controlled observation until fully awake; maintain deep anesthesia throughout to prevent spontaneous movements.

steps.title: Load data into DMA software
steps.instruction: Launch DMA v5.501, choose analysis mode (single file via “File > Open ASI Data File” or batch via the “High Throughput” tab), pick files or a folder for each animal, and verify that the files appear in the Results Table.

steps.title: Set filter and baseline options
steps.instruction: Enable Filter with Cutoff Frequency 70 Hz and Falloff Order 2, enable “Remove Baseline”, and enable “Automatic Inversion” for negative force values.

steps.title: Configure cursor placement
steps.instruction: Select manual cursor definition or automatic placement; for automatic, set Cursor Threshold, Slope Threshold, Baseline Deviation Notification Threshold, and Baseline Slope Notification Threshold as needed, then double‑check and adjust manually if required.

steps.title: Run analysis and review results
steps.instruction: Click “Analyze”; green rows indicate successful analysis, red failed, orange baseline deviation error, yellow baseline slope error, white manual cursor placement, blue cursor order error. Double‑click any row to open the graph, adjust cursors if needed, and click “Update Cursors to Table”.

steps.title: Customize output parameters
steps.instruction: Click “Edit Columns” to add, remove, or modify parameters listed in Table 1 (e.g., Maximum Force, Time to Maximum, Integration, Relaxation Time, etc.), then click “Save Changes”.

steps.title: Export analysis tables
steps.instruction: Click “Export Table” to Excel or “Save Table” to ASCII; save each animal’s results in a dedicated folder with a separate Excel file per animal.

steps.title: Normalize force values
steps.instruction: Calculate relative force for each contraction by dividing the absolute force by the cube root of the animal’s body weight; alternative normalizations (limb length, muscle mass, cross‑sectional area) may be applied as appropriate.

steps.title: Extract additional muscle metrics
steps.instruction: From the processed traces compute fatigue index, contraction time, and force‑frequency relationship parameters; incorporate these metrics into the statistical analysis pipeline according to study objectives.

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Exclude recordings with excessive noise or artifacts. Using Prism 10, run a Shapiro‑Wilk test; if data are Gaussian, conduct a one‑way ANOVA with Dunnett’s post‑hoc test (p < 0.05). For non‑Gaussian data, use Mann‑Whitney U or Kruskal‑Wallis tests. For longitudinal or multifactorial designs, apply mixed‑effects models or repeated‑measures ANOVA.

description:
Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is an X-linked inherited neuromuscular disorder caused by mutations in the DMD gene, leading to a complete loss of functional dystrophin. This results in progressive muscle weakness, loss of ambulation, and ultimately cardiac and respiratory failure.2 Animal models are essential for investigating pathomechanisms, diagnostic procedures3 and potential therapeutic approaches (4; reviewed in5). Due to their pathophysiological similarity to humans, pig models offer a particularly suitable system for studying DMD.6,7,8,9
DMDΔ51–52 pigs exhibit a milder disease phenotype with a partially functional dystrophin and clinically resemble Becker muscular dystrophy (BMD).10 In this protocol, we describe the use of an isometric muscle force measurement system (Aurora A892 Swine Isometric Footplate Test Device) for the functional characterization of skeletal muscle in genetically modified pig models with specific DMD mutations. We examined DMD pigs and BMD pigs, as well as wild-type (WT) controls. This approach enables quantitative analyses of muscle strength, contraction and relaxation dynamics, and muscular endurance through electrical stimulation of the dorsal flexor muscles of the hind limbs.
